purpose: Suite-level trigger eval seed. Each query is labeled with the skill that SHOULD win (expect), or null when no doctrine skill should fire (Resident-stratum-covered, general knowledge, or out of scope). Derive a per-skill run_loop set for skill X as should_trigger = (expect == X); every other query is a should-not-trigger near-miss for X. This is a seed set (~2-3 should-trigger per skill plus boundary near-misses); expand to 8-10 should-trigger per skill before optimizing descriptions.

Added mod 135: authoring-shaped health queries fired 5/5 and 3/3 while this form fired 0/5, and the unloaded answer ('yes, expose /health') is doctrine-wrong and confidently delivered. Deliberately carries no 'web-network' tell — the canonical set's other health query passes only because it has one, which masked this hole.

Answered by healthchecks.md: a non-routed core service declares none, and the field has exactly one consumer (elastic with reverse_proxy: alb). Deliberate near-duplicate of the previous query on subject but not on vocabulary — phrasing robustness on this exact boundary is the defect class mod 135 exists to fix, so the pair is the measurement, not redundancy.
